conclusion.verdict: THREE BOUNDED REPAIRS IMPLEMENTED; REMAINDER ADJUDICATED
conclusion.summary: AppRouter now has three selective tRPC runtime output validators across a closed 421-procedure denominator. The separate routeTrpc compile-time fixture bridge is current and concrete for all 421 paths: zero outputs collapse to never, any, or root unknown, and the stale-payload controls compile only because their @ts-expect-error directives are consumed.
conclusion.noBulkSchemaAction: A zero-validator census is not evidence that 421 new schemas are warranted. Server construction is trusted; runtime output parsing is selective defense at high-consequence wire boundaries.

structuralConsequenceSignals.note: Counts overlap. Signals come from recursive TypeScript-checker traversal of output types and their referenced properties, unions, intersections, and type arguments; they are not text grep classifications.

adjudicationDefinitions.implemented-schema-ready-validation: The procedure now installs its existing canonical runtime schema as a tRPC output parser. Focused controls prove valid output passes and malformed output is rejected; verifyAuth also proves unknown secret-like fields are stripped.
adjudicationDefinitions.owner-decision-required: The boundary is credential-, identity-, raw-token-, or subscription-adjacent and has no ready route output schema. Parser location, strip-versus-strict behavior, and subscription per-emission failure semantics need an owner ruling before product changes.
adjudicationDefinitions.low-consequence-no-payload: The compiler-resolved output is void/undefined. An output validator would validate no payload and is unnecessary absent a separate protocol invariant.
adjudicationDefinitions.high-consequence-candidate-no-confirmed-: The compiler finds a branded or discriminated value somewhere in the output graph, but this audit found no stale runtime payload or serialization defect. It remains a prioritization signal, not proof that a new validator is warranted.
adjudicationDefinitions.ordinary-trusted-output-no-confirmed-def: Concrete JSON-compatible output with no brand/discriminant/non-JSON signal found by the checker. No current defect was confirmed; server construction remains the trust boundary.

implementedSchemaReadyRepairs.reason: Both procedures return CharacterBulkTagResult with branded character ids and a discriminated failure result; both now install the existing canonical schema as their tRPC output parser.

The credential-adjacent diagnostic returns VerifyAuthResult and now installs the existing exact schema as its tRPC output parser. The schema keeps Zod object strip semantics: an unexpected apiKey field is removed before the caller receives the result, while an invalid source discriminator rejects the response.

ownerDecisions.decision: Whether CredentialView should gain a canonical output schema whose parse strips any accidental secret-bearing expansion.
ownerDecisions.reason: CredentialView intentionally excludes plaintext and sealed-secret fields. Adding a route output parser changes the defense boundary and schema ownership, so it requires security review.

ownerDecisions.decision: Whether raw-token and pre-membership invite results need canonical output schemas, and whether those schemas strip or reject excess fields.
ownerDecisions.reason: createInvite returns the raw token exactly once; the other results carry pre-membership identity or roster data. No ready result schema exists.

ownerDecisions.decision: Whether the canonical viewer identity projection needs a runtime output schema in addition to its direct Principal projection.
ownerDecisions.reason: The current producer is a three-field literal projected from the authenticated Principal, so no stale payload was found; schema placement would be a new authority decision.

ownerDecisions.decision: Whether subscription payloads should be validated per emitted frame and what a validation failure does to the stream.
ownerDecisions.reason: The inferred roots are AsyncIterable envelopes. Per-emission parsing and failure behavior are protocol decisions; a procedure-level object schema cannot be added mechanically.
